title: Operator preflight: telemetry, security, and runtime prerequisites
author: Asha Menon
body:
Summary

This page is an operator-facing preflight checklist and acceptance template for Redwood Private (VPC / on‑prem) deployments that focuses on three areas often missed during handoffs: telemetry sampling & retention, security (KMS/HSM and image provenance), and runtime / hardware prerequisites. Use this doc before a customer handoff, pre-install dry runs, or an upgrade window to ensure the deployment will meet SLOs, compliance evidence requirements, and day‑2 observability needs.

Scope

- Applies to all Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem) delivered by the Field Engineering and Private Deployments teams.
- Targets initial commissioning and major upgrades (model swap, runtime upgrade, control plane migration).
- Excludes tenant application-level instrumentation (customer responsibility), but includes our agent/collector and runtime telemetry contracts.

Owners and Contacts

- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (Operational Readiness)
- Primary contact: Asha Menon (Field Engineering) — asha.menon@redwood.ai
- Escalation path: Private Deployments Pager -> eng-sre oncall -> Security oncall

Acceptance Criteria (pre-install)

A deployment is considered ready to go live only when all core items below are checked and evidence artifacts are attached to the ticket: configuration export, sample telemetry traces, KMS policy ARN sample, and a signed image provenance manifest. The ticket must include:

1) Telemetry sample file (1 hour synthetic traffic, gzipped JSON or ndjson).
2) KMS / HSM integration verification (kms-test.log).
3) Hardware inventory (serials + firmware versions).
4) Runtime smoke test output (latency, throughput, kv-cache warmup).

Preflight checklist (detailed)

1) Hardware and runtime environment
- GPU type and count: validated against customer capacity workbook (e.g., 8x A100-80GB per tenant for r1 workload).
- Firmware and BIOS: all NICs and BMCs running firmware >= vendor-min for TLS offload and SR-IOV. Document versions in hw-inventory.csv.
- Host OS and kernel: RHEL 8.6+ or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with kernel >= 5.15. Ensure required modules (nv_peer_mem, rdma) are present if using RoCE.
- Local storage: runtime ephemeral storage >= 500GB for model swap + 2x expected artifact size for safe staging.
- Network MTU: confirm jumbo frames (9000) on data plane where keras/rocksdb replication is used.

2) Network & connectivity
- Control plane egress: allowlist our control plane IPs and TLS fingerprint.
- Model artifact registry access: outbound HTTPS to registry endpoints, TLS1.2+; validate with curl and sha256.
- Tenant subnet design: separate control, data, and operator subnets. Confirm security group rules in vpc-security.yaml.
- Latency requirement: max e2e RTT between operator plane and data plane < 20ms (target), document measured RTTs.

3) Security and key management
- KMS/HSM: confirm key policy supports Envelope Encryption and that our runtime service principal can decrypt keys. Attach kms-test.log demonstrating Encrypt/Decrypt cycle for sample key.
- Key rotation: provide rotation window and automatic rotation script tested in staging.
- Image signing: image manifest must be signed (cosign or equivalent). Provide cosign signature and public key.
- Host attestation: for airgapped sites, TPM attestation report required for first commissioning.
- Secrets injection: confirm secrets delivered via CSI driver or cloud KMS integration; do not persist keys in plain text in runtime config.

4) Telemetry, sampling, and retention (operator contract)
- Telemetry components: runtime-metrics (Prometheus), traces (OpenTelemetry), logs (structured JSON to fluentd/forwarder).
- Sampling strategy: default is adaptive sampling with three tiers:
  - Critical traces (errors, fallback events): 100% sampled
  - High-latency user requests (> 300ms): 20% sampled
  - Background / debug traces: 1% sampled
- Telemetry sampling config (example):
  telemetry:
    traces:
      sampling_strategy: adaptive
      rules:
        - name: critical-errors
          match: "span.attributes.status == 'error'"
          sample_rate: 1.0
        - name: high-latency
          match: "span.duration_ms > 300"
          sample_rate: 0.2
        - name: default-low
          match: "*"
          sample_rate: 0.01
- Retention policy: default local retention for raw traces = 72h, archived nightly to customer S3 for 365 days when requested. Logs: 30 days hot, 365 days cold (compressed). Metrics: 90 days 1s resolution, 3 years aggregated.
- Privacy & PII: ensure PII redaction rules are applied at the collector; attach redaction.yaml demonstrating regex rules and PII tokenization examples.

5) Observability acceptance tests (pre-install smoke)
- Generate synthetic workload of 100 qps for 15 minutes that includes model-compute-heavy and cache-hit patterns. Collect: Prometheus scrape, OTLP traces, sample logs.
- Expected telemetry outputs:
  - Prometheus: key metrics visible (inference_latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_utilization).
  - Traces: at least 10 error traces, and representative sampled high-latency traces.
  - Logs: structured logs with fields: request_id, tenant_id, model_name, latency_ms, status.
- Attach synthetic_telemetry_YYYYMMDD.ndjson to ticket.

6) IAM and operator permissions
- Operator service principal permissions: minimal set required to perform runtime operations (pull images, start/stop pods, read secrets). Provide example AWS IAM policy snippet or GCP IAM role mapping.
- Access review: confirm RBAC role binding for operator, and an operator-only emergency-control-plane role for rapid rollback.
- Audit logging: ensure operator actions are logged to a tamper-evident audit sink (CloudWatch/Stackdriver or on‑prem ELK).

7) Model artifacts and compatibility
- Model quantization profile: pre-agreed quantization profiles listed in quantization-profiles.csv.
- Artifact schema: model artifact must include manifest.json (fields: name, version, framework, sha256, tokenizer_sha256, prod_compat_matrix).
- Warm-start validation: runtime must be able to warm KV cache within 120s for the working set. Provide warm-start test output.

Upgrade & rollback prerequisites (before any major upgrade)

- Snapshot: take control-plane and runtime state snapshot; label with ticket id and time.
- KV-cache checkpoint: the operator must create a consistent KV checkpoint export.
- Compatibility gate: run offline compatibility matrix tool against the new runtime and attached models; record report.
- Canary plan: minimum 5% of traffic to canary group with automatic rollback criteria: p95 latency increase > 20% sustained for 5 minutes OR error rate increase > 1% absolute.
- Rollback playbook: ensure operator has prepopulated rollback_playbook.md in ticket with commands and evidence locations.

Post-install day‑2 observability and SLOs (operator checks within first 24h)

- SLOs to validate:
  - Availability (serving endpoint): 99.95% per tenant for the first 7 days
  - Latency: p95 < 450ms for small models; p95 < 1s for large models (documented per-tenant).
  - Kv-cache hit rate: > 85% during steady-state.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - inference_latency_p95 > threshold -> paged (P1 if > 30% above target for 10m)
  - error_rate > 0.5% -> investigate (P2)
  - detached_kv_cache_nodes > 0 -> oncall (P1 if > 1 node)
- Evidence collection: attach first 24h dashboard snapshot and a summary.csv with metrics aggregated by hour.

Compliance evidence and artifacts to collect

- KMS policy export (kms-policy.json) and kms-test.log
- Audit sink export for operator actions (audit-export.tar.gz)
- Signed image manifest and cosign public key (image-manifest.json, signature.sig, cosign.pub)
- Telemetry sample archive (synthetic_telemetry_YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz)
- Hardware inventory and firmware bill of materials (hw-inventory.csv)

Operator runbook snippets (copy into operator ticket)

1) Quick rollback (stateless control-plane config rollback)
- Commands (example):
  - kubectl -n redwood apply -f rollback/control-plane-config-<ticket>.yaml
  - ./operator-tools/evict-heavy-tenants --grace-period 90s --target-tenant <id>
  - ./scripts/restore-kv-checkpoint --checkpoint s3://evidence/<ticket>/kv-checkpoint.tgz
2) KMS rebind test
- Commands (example):
  - aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://sample.cipher --key-id <customer-key-id> --output text > /tmp/decrypted
  - systemctl restart redwood-agent && journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 | grep KMS

Appendix: example telemetry redaction rule (redaction.yaml)

- name: email-redaction
  match: "[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+"
  replace: "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
- name: credit-card
  match: "\b(?:\d[ -]*?){13,16}\b"
  replace: "[REDACTED_CC]"

Appendix: sample model artifact manifest (manifest.json snippet)

{
  "name": "redwood-open-7b",
  "version": "2027-02-14",
  "framework": "pytorch",
  "sha256": "<hex-sha256>",
  "quantization_profile": "q4a"
}

Notes and best practices

- Treat telemetry as first-class evidence for SLOs and compliance. Keep one synthetic telemetry run for each major upgrade window.
- Use adaptive sampling to keep trace volumes bounded while preserving signal for anomalies.
- Store all evidence artifacts alongside the customer ticket and mark required retention windows in the ticket metadata.

Related pages and further reading

- Deployment commissioning playbook (internal): link to internal playbook for step-by-step operator tasks.
- Field operator training deck: attend the monthly session for hands-on runthroughs.
